title: Proof (wellness): testing the category's default style, and how to set the test up
hook: In wellness, aspirational content is the default. One brand tested it.
caption:
In wellness, aspirational content is the default. One brand tested it.
The result is published, and the test design is yours to copy.

The numbers for this Ayurvedic supplements D2C brand (anonymised, on galvor.ai): a 2.6× uplift versus aspirational content, +135% hold rate and +91% RoAS.

This does not mean aspirational content is bad. It means every category has a default style that nobody questions, and the default deserves one fair test.

The slides show how to set that test up on your own account.

If you would like us to find the default in your category, we will decode it free. Details are in the first comment.

slides.headline: A supplements brand tested its category's *default style*
slides.sub: Anonymised client · results published on galvor.ai

slides.headline: Name your category's *default*
slides.body:
Open the ad libraries of ten brands in your category and note the style most of them share.

In wellness it is often the calm, aspirational lifestyle shot. In yours it may be the founder story or the before and after.

slides.headline: Make its *opposite*, with the same message
slides.body:
Keep the promise, the offer and the product identical.

Change only the style. If the default is polished, shoot plain. If it is aspirational, show the routine as it really looks.

slides.headline: Price the *difference*
slides.body:
Run both for a full fortnight at similar spend.

Compare hold rate and cost per order. Then write one line: in our category, this style costs this much more or less per order.
